summary: ```markdown # CLO Techniques Workshop - Custom Object Button ## Introduction In this workshop, we'll explore the process of creating a flower model in CLO and how to set it up for optimal use with buttons. This guide will walk you through the necessary steps to ensure your model is properly configured and exported. ## Creating the Flower Model To begin, open the software and create a good flower model. ### Placement of the Model - The model must be placed at the **origin**. - In the 3D window, you will notice a **floor** with two vertical lines marking the **origin** at the center of the x-axis and y-axis. - Ensure that the flower is placed **flat on the origin** of the floor, as this is the point where the button will point to the top of the board. ## Exporting the Model Next, export the model to **OPT**. - **Name** the file and then click **Save**. - You will see an export window. Choose **all panels**. - Here, you must choose a **single target**. The merging option is not a concern in this instance. - Select the option after the merging, and do not select **Unified UV coordinates** since this flower model has no texture. - The flag color does not need to be saved; choose the option after that. - Save the zip file with the texture, which will be saved as a **compression bag**. - Note that the last option cannot be selected because the flower itself is white and lacks texture. ## Adding a Button Once the model is exported, find a well-preserved compression bag and proceed to add a button. ### Button Configuration - Choose the button and find the **plus sign** next to it. - Press the symbol to connect it with the button material. - Click the **plus sign** to add additional settings. - On the left, you will see the corresponding settings, and on the right is the **preview window**. ## Setting Up the OPT Next, we need to add the OPT file. - Click the **browse** button and then click **open**. - You will see a grid with only **two grids**, making it easy to select. ### Selecting Targets If you initially exported the OPT and did not select a single target but multiple targets, you will need to select all targets. - You should see the option to **select all** multiple times. This is crucial because if you do not select just one target, the flower will be separated into several flower spots, resulting in dozens of grid spots which complicates the layout. ### Naming the Model At the top of the interface, you can rename your model. For instance, name it **Airline**. ## Adjusting Dimensions Now, let’s adjust the view value and dimensions of the flower. ### Size Adjustments - It’s better to change the size according to the requirements. - For example, reduce the width of the flower to **10**, and adjust the thickness of the bottom to **4**. - Keep the width and thickness in relative proportion to ensure that the flower does not deform. - Set the width to **15 mm** and the thickness to **6.2 mm**. ### Axis Orientation - The axis orientation is converted, and there is no need for further adjustments at this point. - When exporting the OPT, ensure that the flower is placed at the origin to align all axis directions correctly. ## Final Confirmation Click to confirm your settings and adjustments. ## Using the Twist Tool Finally, utilize the option to move the **twist tool**. - Select the front and middle twist, and apply a new twist according to the material and color of the twist. ```
